clue.text: Original act of trade union male, a versatile worker

indicators.note: something original is novel, made new, so the words act of are rearranged into fresh order

explanation.surface: A union man's pioneering deed earns him a reputation as an all-rounder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like an adjective for 'act' but is the anagram signal; the comma after 'male' marks where the definition starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, a handyman of many tasks.

clue.text: Dry wine for Charles de Gaulle, for example

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A dry wine fit for the French general.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles de Gaulle is not the general here but the Paris terminal named after him; 'Dry' is a verb, not a description of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle is the main international hub serving Paris, an example of a place where planes land.

clue.text: Follow court activity of sporting outfit

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
a suit is a lawsuit, the business of a law court

explanation.surface: Tracking a tennis match while dressed for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court activity' suggests tennis but means a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose jacket and trousers worn for athletic training or leisure.

clue.text: Foreign accent a Spanish gentleman, for example, has

definitions.text: Foreign accent a Spanish gentleman, for example, has

parts.words: Foreign accent a Spanish gentleman, for example, has
parts.note: reads like the way a Spaniard speaks English, but means the written mark over the n in the Spanish word for gentleman, señor

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman speaks with a foreign accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent is a written diacritic, not a manner of speech: señor carries a wavy mark over its n.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy diacritic over the Spanish n marks a palatal nasal sound, an accent mark in print.

clue.text: Hero, a moderate

parts.note: the letters at the centre of the phrase the road, read as one run, spell out this word

explanation.surface: A hero who is nonetheless a moderate figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, takes the middle of THE ROAD, t-HERO-ad, giving the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-of-the-road position avoids extremes, the stance of a centrist.

clue.text: Reason to include one piece of writing in fantasy

indicators.note: the word for reason is made to include, that is hold inside, the other pieces

parts.note: why means reason, as in the whys and wherefores
I is the Roman numeral one
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A writer's justification for slipping some fantasy into the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' looks like logic, but it is the question word that asks for one; 'to include' wraps it around one and the manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playful, fanciful notion, a flight of imagination.

clue.text: One prepared to bet, with joker and two queens

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a wit

indicators.note: two asks for the abbreviation for queen to be written down twice in succession

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A card player holding the joker and a pair of queens is ready to stake money.
explanation.walkthrough: The cards are a red herring: the joker is a WAG and each queen is ER (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: A wagerer is a punter, someone who stakes money on an outcome.

clue.text: In communication by radio, I land in Asia

definitions.meaning: in the radio spelling alphabet the letter I is called by this code word
a large country of South Asia

explanation.surface: A radio operator sends a message as he touches down in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic code word for the letter I is also the name of the South Asian republic.

clue.text: Enjoy embracing one rescuer

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the word for enjoy wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to savour something is to enjoy it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Relishing a hug from the person who saved you.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside SAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A saviour is one who saves others from danger, a deliverer.

clue.text: Callas initially cut out for part in opera

indicators.note: the opening letter of the soprano's first name is cut out, so only the rest remains

parts.note: Maria Callas, the celebrated soprano

explanation.surface: The diva Callas was well suited to a role in opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out for' reads as 'suited to', but 'initially cut out' removes the M from MARIA, Callas's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song within an opera.

clue.text: As negotiator of tax relief, she was barely up for it

definitions.text: As negotiator of tax relief, she was barely up for it

parts.words: As negotiator of tax relief, she was barely up for it
parts.note: a woman who won lower taxes for her townsfolk by riding through the streets naked, barely clothed, on horseback, so 'up for it' means mounted

explanation.surface: A tax campaigner was barely keen on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the Coventry noblewoman rode naked through the town so her husband would lift a harsh tax; 'barely' means naked and 'up' means on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century countess of the legend bargained with her husband for tax relief by riding unclothed.

clue.text: His wares are bound to be marketable

definitions.text: His wares are bound to be marketable

parts.words: His wares are bound to be marketable
parts.note: bound seems to mean certain, but the goods are literally bound volumes, put up for sale in a shop

explanation.surface: A trader whose goods are sure to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but the wares are bound in covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells printed volumes, which are bound in covers.

clue.text: A doctor's or a prophet's work

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; with the possessive it gives MO's

explanation.surface: Is it the work of a physician or of a prophet?
explanation.walkthrough: A + MO'S (a medical officer's). The Old Testament book is named after the prophet who wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Amos in the Old Testament carries the words of a minor prophet.

clue.text: Corpulent, with weight made public

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds
out means revealed, made known

explanation.surface: A fat person's weight is publicly revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone (ST) is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavy, thickset build, a polite word for fat.

clue.text: Woo eccentric, such as Jack

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a card is an eccentric or comical person

explanation.surface: Jack is an odd fellow who goes courting.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a playing card, not a man; 'card' means an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is one of the picture cards in a pack, alongside king and queen.

clue.text: Tea coming by post, in old-fashioned protective covering

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
mail is the post

explanation.surface: Tea arrives by post at a quaint old place.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlinked metal rings worn as armour by medieval soldiers.

clue.text: Tiny trace destroyed, no doubt

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tiny trace was wiped out, without question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyed' rearranges TINY TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainty is the state of being sure, the absence of any question.

clue.text: Examine closely as I cry loudly in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard by the listener, so the pieces are said aloud

parts.note: the letter I is said like the word for the organ of sight; to bawl is to cry loudly, and it is said like a round toy

explanation.surface: I examine things closely while wailing within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hearing' makes I sound like EYE and BAWL sound like BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to stare at it hard, inspecting it.

clue.text: Briefly deflected air down

indicators.note: deflected means turned aside from its course, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Air pushed downwards, described in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deflected' rearranges AIR DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Summing up concisely, to put it shortly.

clue.text: Follow hunter, for example

definitions.meaning: to keep an eye on, observe
a hunter is a pocket timepiece with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: Track the hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to keep an eye on it, and a hunter is a type of pocket timepiece with a cover.

clue.text: Constant rush to punish

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant in physics, such as the speed of light
to hasten is to rush

explanation.surface: A constant hurry to discipline someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or correct someone to subdue them.

clue.text: Details of courses available from people with university

parts.note: men means people, persons

explanation.surface: Course details on offer from staff at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests degree courses at the university, but they are meal courses.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes, starter to dessert, a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Complete, say

explanation.surface: Finish, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means absolute, and as a verb means to voice words.

clue.text: Scot 'ad one bairn ganging agley

indicators.note: Scots for going wrong, from the Burns line about schemes that gang aft agley, so the letters go awry

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's plans for the child he'd had went awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ganging agley' (Scots: going astray, from Burns's 'To a Mouse') rearranges 'AD ONE BAIRN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Aberdeen, a city in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Suit ready in Japan for senior member

parts.note: do means suit, be adequate, as in that will do
ready is slang for cash, and the yen is Japan's money

explanation.surface: A suit made up in Japan for the oldest member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash (ready money); in Japan that is YEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a group.

clue.text: Science associated with gourmets, primarily

parts.note: a study chiefly pursued by lovers of fine food: the art and science of good eating

explanation.surface: A discipline mostly linked to lovers of fine food.
explanation.walkthrough: A plain description: 'primarily' means chiefly, not first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of food and cookery, the art of eating well.

clue.text: Aesthetically gifted person, initially penniless

indicators.note: the word must go without its initial letter, the first one, as if broke

parts.note: a party is a person, as in the guilty party

explanation.surface: An artistic person who starts out broke.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY loses its first letter, P (penny).
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone with artistic leanings or pretensions.

clue.text: Lid for potty that's excessively ornate

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the words lid for go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A fancy lid for a child's potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' rearranges LID FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid describes elaborate decoration, flowery to excess.

clue.text: Hanging down from end of rod, fishing

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken here from rod

parts.note: angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A line hangs from the tip of a fishing rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangling means suspended loosely, swinging from above.
